title: Keith McArthur:
headline: Everyone says pharma is bad. CureGRIN’s CEO tells the people building a GRIN treatment why parents of a child with a rare disease see it differently, what the families are doing on their own, and who they are counting on.
story: Keith McArthur, standing at the window side of the room on 8 Oct, gives the GRIN Therapeutics team the parents’ view in one short answer. He names the common feeling first, pharma is bad, then turns it: a parent of a child with a rare disease gets a different view. He describes the families: some raising money on their own for preclinical work toward an ASO for their own kid, many so busy caring for their kid that hoping is all they can do. Then the line to the room: you are so important to us for our potential to get to treatments and cures.

For donors and partners. Hopeful, never somber. No drug name, no trial name, no dates. Never a hint that a cure is near or that anyone is at fault. This is a different cut from the hero 13277146397 (the trial and “you are my heroes”), the Seventh Family 13277142181 and the Carter story 13319123571: none of those use the C5226 clip.

Loops: L1 “Why would a rare-disease dad say pharma is not bad?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:04 (“get a different view”). L2 “Who are these families counting on?” opens at 0:00 and closes in the BUTTON (“you are so important to us”). Stakes: families with no networks, no resources and no time, hoping something comes along for their kid.
